{"id": "54e5e41c-f5b2-4b8d-8208-c08eed07ece1", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The instance ID you gave, `i-1234567890abcdef0_1`, isn't a valid ID. EC2 rejected it as malformed, and it looks like a placeholder. I couldn't check the instance's disk, so what follows comes from the error text.

## What's wrong
`[Errno 28] No space left on device: /var/cache/dnf` means the filesystem holding `/var/cache/dnf` has run out of space. On Amazon Linux 2023 that is usually the root volume, which is often 8 GB by default. `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` runs `dnf` for the install, and `dnf` needs room to download packages and metadata. It couldn't write its cache, so the Install operation failed. Patching isn't broken. The disk is full.

It could also be inodes rather than bytes. A volume can show free space and still hit this error if it has run out of inodes.

## How to confirm
Connect with Session Manager and run:
```
df -h /  /var  /var/cache
df -i /
sudo du -xh /var --max-depth=2 | sort -rh | head -20
sudo du -xh / --max-depth=1 | sort -rh | head
```
Common causes are old logs in `/var/log` or the journal, old dnf caches, application data or core dumps, and old kernels.

## Quick fix (free space)
```
sudo dnf clean all
sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=100M
sudo dnf remove --oldinstallonly --setopt installonly_limit=2 kernel-core   # only if old kernels are piling up
```
Then remove large old logs or temp files you identified with `du`.

## Durable fix (grow the volume)
1. Take a snapshot of the root volume first.
2. Increase the size in EC2 (Volumes → Modify), or run `aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id <vol-id> --size <GiB>`. Wait until the state is `optimizing` or `completed`.
3. On the instance, extend the partition and filesystem. Amazon Linux 2023 root is XFS on a partition, so run:
```
sudo growpart /dev/nvme0n1 1
sudo xfs_growfs -d /
```
(Use `lsblk` to confirm the device name.)

## Then re-run patching
Re-run `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` with Operation=Install. A good target is at least 20–30% free space before the next patch window. To catch this earlier, run the CloudWatch agent and alarm on `disk_used_percent`.

If you send me the correct instance ID, I can look at its volume size and attached volumes. I can also help work out why the disk filled up.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
